content.text: This issue may potentially be resolved by changing the "auto-registration" of the beans/classes via @Component mentioned in this ticket's description with explicit bean definitions in the repo.xml.

Since the AccessRoles.accessRoleProvider is only null when using WebAC, I was thinking if there is a way to check it before injecting the fedora:hasAccessRoles property into the model for a node, that should keep it from appearing.
Can you please add a link or two to lines in source code?

to the auth-repo.xml for RBACL and XACML in fcrepo-webapp-plus. Does the name of the bean matter?
, that is what I had in mind as well.

When any of the following Authorization modules are configured,

..a "fedora:hasAccessRoles" property [1] is created on new resources and a number of RBACL node-types [2] are registered. The "hasAccessRoles" service makes sense for RBACL and XACML, but not for WebAC. Since WebAC is the authorization module which we are encouraging the community to move towards, having the "hasAccessRoles" service exposed is incorrect and confusing.
This task is to ensure that the "hasAccessRoles" property and the RBACL node-types are not included with WebAC is configured.

comments.body: This issue may potentially be resolved by changing the "auto-registration" of the beans/classes via @Component mentioned in this ticket's description with explicit bean definitions in the repo.xml.

Since the AccessRoles.accessRoleProvider is only null when using WebAC, I was thinking if there is a way to check it before injecting the fedora:hasAccessRoles property into the model for a node, that should keep it from appearing.
Can you please add a link or two to lines in source code?

I'm thinking a check here to make sure there is an access roles provider: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-rbacl/blob/master/fcrepo-auth-roles-common/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/roles/common/AccessRolesResources.java#L57

Why wouldn't you simply remove this line: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-rbacl/blob/master/fcrepo-auth-roles-common/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/roles/common/AccessRolesResources.java#L42

and then add the component to the relevant Spring configuration in rbacl and xacml?

Do you have access to AccessRoles.accessRolesProvider from https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-rbacl/blob/master/fcrepo-auth-roles-common/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/roles/common/AccessRolesResources.java#L43 ?

Unknown Your approach sounds more transparent. I'm still trying to figure out my bearings in Spring. Is this correct? Removing the @Component annotation would keep the system from automatically instantiating a AccessRolesResources bean, so I would add something like <bean name="accessRolesResources" class="org.fcrepo.auth.roles.common.AccessRolesResources"/> to the auth-repo.xml for RBACL and XACML in fcrepo-webapp-plus. Does the name of the bean matter?
Unknown, that is what I had in mind as well.

Peter Matthew Eichman That is correct. You'd want to add that bean in the following places (I might be missing a few spots – but this will get you started):

For RBACL:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-rbacl/blob/master/fcrepo-auth-roles-basic/src/test/resources/spring-test/repo.xml

https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/blob/master/src/rbacl/webapp/WEB-INF/classes/spring/auth-repo.xml

For XACML:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/blob/master/src/webac/webapp/WEB-INF/classes/spring/auth-repo.xml

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-xacml/blob/master/src/test/resources/spring-test/repo.xml

Unknown That is working so far. I've also added a null check around the code at https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-rbacl/blob/2039ac82bcff5d419dcc91f12cf2f49af268a58f/fcrepo-auth-roles-common/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/auth/roles/common/AccessRoles.java#L140 that will respond with a 404 if someone requests fcr:accessroles but the accessRolesProvider is null, instead of the current behavior of throwing a null pointer exception. Hopefully users would not be blindly appending "/fcr:accessroles" to repository URLs, but in case it happens I figure it is better to check and return a sensible response than just letting an exception through.

Next up, I will take a look at adding some integration tests to check for the existence (or not) of the "fcr:accessroles" resource.
